book.title: User guide
book.description: How to use AI Scientist from asking a research question to reading sourced answers and exporting a report

topics.title: About this guide
topics.summary: This guide explains how to use AI Scientist, a web assistant for academic research. You ask a research question in Thai or English. The system plans search terms, searches scholarly sources, writes an answer from what it finds, and checks that the DOI, PMID or arXiv ID of each reference exists. You can then turn the answer into a report.

sections.heading: What is this guide
sections.body:
This guide explains how to use AI Scientist, a web assistant for academic research. You ask a research question in Thai or English. The system plans search terms, searches scholarly sources, writes an answer from what it finds, and checks that the DOI, PMID or arXiv ID of each reference exists. You can then turn the answer into a report.

Each chapter starts from what the reader wants to do and follows the real screens. Button and menu names in quotation marks match what you see on screen. The pictures use invented test data, not real user data.

sections.heading: Reading order
sections.body:
- Start with [Get started](/docs/getting-started), then read [Ask a research question](/docs/ask-a-question) and [Open the sources of an answer](/docs/read-sources)
- If you have your own documents or data, see [Ask about PDF documents](/docs/ask-documents) and [Analyze a data file](/docs/analyze-data)
- To turn an answer into a report, see [Create a report document from an answer](/docs/create-report)
- Before you use an answer for real, read [What the system covers and what you must check](/docs/limits-and-safety) and [Where your data is kept and sent](/docs/data-and-privacy)
- When a problem message appears, see [Common problems and fixes](/docs/faq)

sections.heading: Information pages on the website
sections.body: The first page of the system has menus “How it works”, “FAQ” and “Product” that describe the system in brief. You do not need them to work in the chat. The “Guide” menu on the first page still says that the guide is in development.

topics.title: Get started
topics.summary: AI Scientist works right away in the browser. You do not need to register or sign in. This page takes you from the first page to the chat screen, the main place to ask research questions, read answers and browse files.

sections.heading: What is getting started
sections.body:
AI Scientist works right away in the browser. You do not need to register or sign in. This page takes you from the first page to the chat screen, the main place to ask research questions, read answers and browse files.

![The AI Scientist chat screen](/manual/en/chat-home.webp#1280x800 "The AI Scientist chat screen")

The chat screen has two parts. The left bar has the **New chat** button, the **Projects** list, the **Search chats** box and the menus **My files**, **Trash** and **Settings**. The middle is the question box with buttons for the research mode and the research field.

sections.heading: How to get started
sections.body:
1. Click **Get started** at the top right

   ![Click Get started at the top right](/manual/en/start-open-1.webp#1280x800)

2. The chat screen opens with the question box

   ![The chat screen opens with the question box](/manual/en/start-open-2.webp#1280x800)

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.body:
- The left bar shows a connection status such as “Online · shared database”. See [Where your data is kept and sent](/docs/data-and-privacy) for what it means
- The question box shows a faint sample question. Press the Tab key to put the sample question in the box, or click a sample card below it
- You can ask in Thai or English. Change the language of the screen in [Change the language and theme](/docs/language-theme)
- The system answers only scientific research questions. Read the limits in [What the system covers and what you must check](/docs/limits-and-safety)
- Click **Hide sidebar** to hide the left bar and make room for the work area

sections.heading: Problems and fixes
sections.body:
- **Problem:** “Something went wrong”  
  **Fix:** The page failed to render, but your chats stored in this browser are not affected. Click **Try again**
- **Problem:** “Page not found”  
  **Fix:** The link may be wrong or the page has moved. Click **Go to chat**

sections.heading: Related questions
sections.body:
- [Ask a research question](/docs/ask-a-question)
- [Common problems and fixes](/docs/faq)

topics.title: Ask a research question
topics.summary: The question box on the chat screen takes a research question of up to 2000 characters. Two buttons next to the send button choose how the system works.

sections.heading: What is asking a research question
sections.body:
The question box on the chat screen takes a research question of up to 2000 characters. Two buttons next to the send button choose how the system works.

- Mode button: **Deep research** plans search terms and searches scholarly sources, **General search** uses fewer search terms, and **Answer research** answers from results already found in that chat without searching again. You can choose it once the chat has an answer
- Field button: **All fields** or the field that fits your topic, such as Medicine. The system then picks sources that fit better
- While it works, the screen shows the stages (plan, search, write, check references) and papers appearing as they are found. Click **Stop** to stop the work at any time

sections.heading: How to ask a research question
sections.body:
1. Click the question box and enter your research question

   ![Click the question box and enter your research question](/manual/en/ask-flow-1.webp#1280x800)

2. Click the research mode button

   ![Click the research mode button](/manual/en/ask-flow-2.webp#1280x800)

3. Choose a mode from the list

   ![Choose a mode from the list](/manual/en/ask-flow-3.webp#1280x800)

4. Click the research field button

   ![Click the research field button](/manual/en/ask-flow-4.webp#1280x800)

5. Choose a field from the list

   ![Choose a field from the list](/manual/en/ask-flow-5.webp#1280x800)

6. Click the paper-plane send button

   ![Click the paper-plane send button](/manual/en/ask-flow-6.webp#1280x800)

![Ask a question and get the answer](/manual/en/ask-video.mp4#cc "Ask a question and get the answer")

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.body:
- Press Enter to send the question, and hold Shift while pressing Enter to start a new line
- In **Deep research** mode the system proposes the search plan for you to check before it starts. See [Review and edit the plan before searching](/docs/review-plan). If you turned this step off, it starts at once. See [Turn the plan review on or off](/docs/plan-setting)
- The system searches with up to 5 search terms per question, and each search term can take up to 5 minutes
- When several people use the system, work waits in a queue, and the screen shows your place and the estimated wait
- If you attach a file, the send button acts differently. See [Ask about PDF documents](/docs/ask-documents) and [Analyze a data file](/docs/analyze-data)
- The answer comes from a language model, so check the sources before you use it. See [Open the sources of an answer](/docs/read-sources)

sections.heading: Problems and fixes
sections.body:
- **Problem:** “Question is longer than 2000 characters”  
  **Fix:** Shorten the question and send it again
- **Problem:** “You already have the maximum jobs waiting. Wait for one to finish.”  
  **Fix:** Wait for the earlier work to finish, or click **Stop** on it, then send the new question
- **Problem:** “The queue is full. Try again shortly.”  
  **Fix:** Wait a moment and send again
- **Problem:** “Could not send the run. The server is not ready. Try again.”  
  **Fix:** Send the question again. If it stays the same, see [Common problems and fixes](/docs/faq)
- **Problem:** “The run failed. You can retry.”  
  **Fix:** Click **Try again**

topics.title: Review and edit the plan before searching
topics.summary: In Deep research mode, after you send a question, the system proposes a Research plan (editable): a list of search terms, one per item, each with a short instruction about what to take from the papers found. It does not search until you click Start search. Use this when you want the search to fit better, to drop a term you do not want, or to add a term of your own.

sections.heading: What is reviewing the plan
sections.body:
In **Deep research** mode, after you send a question, the system proposes a **Research plan (editable)**: a list of search terms, one per item, each with a short instruction about what to take from the papers found. It does not search until you click **Start search**. Use this when you want the search to fit better, to drop a term you do not want, or to add a term of your own.

**General search** and **Answer research** modes do not wait at this step.

sections.heading: How to review and edit the plan
sections.body:
1. The system shows the proposed research plan with each search term

   ![The system shows the proposed research plan with each search term](/manual/en/plan-flow-1.webp#1280x800)

2. Click **Edit plan**

   ![Click Edit plan](/manual/en/plan-flow-2.webp#1280x800)

3. Change the text in **Search term** as needed

   ![Change the text in Search term as needed](/manual/en/plan-flow-3.webp#1280x800)

4. Click **Add search** to search for one more term

   ![Click Add search to search for one more term](/manual/en/plan-flow-4.webp#1280x800)

5. Click **Start search**

   ![Click Start search](/manual/en/plan-flow-5.webp#1280x800)

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.body:
- Search terms must be in English only, up to 5 of them, and at least 1 must remain
- The **Extra instructions (optional)** box says what you want from the papers found. You can leave it empty
- Remove a term with the trash can button at the end of its row
- Click **Cancel** if you do not want to search
- If the results are thin, the system may add search terms by itself while it searches and say so with “Plan adjusted”
- If you do not want to review the plan every time, turn it off in [Turn the plan review on or off](/docs/plan-setting)

sections.heading: Problems and fixes
sections.body:
- **Problem:** “Search terms must be in English only”  
  **Fix:** Change the term to English, then click **Start search** again
- **Problem:** “Enter a search term”  
  **Fix:** Enter a term in the empty box, or remove that row

sections.heading: Related questions
sections.body:

- [Turn the plan review on or off](/docs/plan-setting)

topics.title: Open the sources of an answer
topics.summary: Every sentence in the answer that cites research has a source label, such as “Yucheng et al. 2023” (the first author and the year). Click a label to open a details panel on the right. It shows the authors, the year, the source, which database found it, the DOI, the identifier check, and the quoted evidence with a result saying whether the abstract supports the statement. Use it when you want to check a sentence before you cite it.

sections.heading: What is opening the sources
sections.body:
Every sentence in the answer that cites research has a source label, such as “Yucheng et al. 2023” (the first author and the year). Click a label to open a details panel on the right. It shows the authors, the year, the source, which database found it, the DOI, the identifier check, and the quoted evidence with a result saying whether the abstract supports the statement. Use it when you want to check a sentence before you cite it.

The **Sources** tab above the answer lists all the sources of that answer.

sections.heading: How to open the sources of an answer
sections.body:
1. In the answer, click the name of a cited source, such as Yucheng et al. 2023

   ![In the answer, click the name of a cited source, such as Yucheng et al. 2023](/manual/en/source-flow-1.webp#1280x800)

2. The source details open on the right

   ![The source details open on the right](/manual/en/source-flow-2.webp#1280x800)

3. Click the button that closes the source details

   ![Click the button that closes the source details](/manual/en/source-flow-3.webp#1280x800)

4. Click the **Sources** tab above the answer

   ![Click the Sources tab above the answer](/manual/en/source-flow-4.webp#1280x800)

5. The system lists every source of the answer

   ![The system lists every source of the answer](/manual/en/source-flow-5.webp#1280x800)

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.body:
- The identifier check only confirms that the DOI, PMID or arXiv ID exists. It does not confirm that the paper supports the sentence in the answer
- The quote check has 4 results: **Supported by the abstract**, **Partly supported by the abstract**, **Not supported by the abstract** and **No quote found**. The reviewer reads only the abstract, not the full text
- Click **Open source** at the end of the panel to read the original, and check it yourself before you use it
- An answer from your own PDF documents uses numbers such as [1] and [2] at the end of sentences. Click one to see the page and the text in the document. See [Ask about PDF documents](/docs/ask-documents)
- Records from some public databases (when present) appear under **Database records** below the answer

sections.heading: Problems and fixes
sections.body:
- **Problem:** “Could not confirm this reference exists”  
  **Fix:** The system did not find this identifier in the checking sources. Look for the paper yourself before you use it, and do not cite it unchecked
- **Problem:** “Could not be checked right now (the service did not answer)”  
  **Fix:** The checking service did not answer. This does not mean the paper is fake. Wait a moment and ask again, or check the identifier yourself
- **Problem:** “No identifier (DOI/PMID) to check”  
  **Fix:** This item has no DOI, PMID or arXiv ID to check. Search for it by its title
- **Problem:** “No abstract to check against”  
  **Fix:** The system has no abstract for this paper. Open the original and read it yourself

sections.body:

- [What the system covers and what you must check](/docs/limits-and-safety)

topics.title: Copy an answer and export the references
topics.summary: Below a finished answer there is a row of answer tools. Use it to copy the answer text, download the provenance file, and download the references as BibTeX or RIS to import into a reference manager such as Zotero or EndNote. The provenance file says which model, instructions and sources the answer used. The Regenerate answer button in the same row asks the same question again.

sections.heading: What is copying and exporting
sections.body: Below a finished answer there is a row of answer tools. Use it to copy the answer text, download the provenance file, and download the references as BibTeX or RIS to import into a reference manager such as Zotero or EndNote. The provenance file says which model, instructions and sources the answer used. The **Regenerate answer** button in the same row asks the same question again.

sections.heading: How to copy an answer and export the references
sections.body:
1. Scroll to the end of the answer to find the answer tools

   ![Scroll to the end of the answer to find the answer tools](/manual/en/ref-flow-1.webp#1280x800)

2. Click the copy answer icon

   ![Click the copy answer icon](/manual/en/ref-flow-2.webp#1280x800)

3. Click BibTeX to download the references for a reference manager

   ![Click BibTeX to download the references for a reference manager](/manual/en/ref-flow-3.webp#1280x800)

4. Click RIS to download the references in the other format

   ![Click RIS to download the references in the other format](/manual/en/ref-flow-4.webp#1280x800)

5. Click the download provenance icon to keep a file that names the model, the instructions and the sources used

   ![Click the download provenance icon to keep a file that names the model, the instructions and the sources used](/manual/en/ref-flow-5.webp#1280x800)

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.body:
- The exported references are built from the sources of the answer. Check the titles and years against the originals before you use them in your writing
- The provenance file keeps the question, the answer and the references with their identifier check, but not the abstracts of the papers
- The download provenance button appears only on answers that have provenance data. Some older answers may not have it
- To turn the answer into a document, see [Create a report document from an answer](/docs/create-report)

sections.heading: Problems and fixes
sections.body:
- **Problem:** “Copy failed”  
  **Fix:** The browser did not allow copying. Select the text in the answer and copy it yourself

sections.heading: Related questions
sections.body:
- [Open the sources of an answer](/docs/read-sources)
- [Create a report document from an answer](/docs/create-report)

topics.title: Ask about PDF documents
topics.summary: You can attach 1 to 5 of your own PDF files and ask about what is in them. When you attach a PDF, the system switches to From documents mode and answers only from the attached documents. It does not search other research and does not use the research field. The answer has numbers such as [1] and [2] at the end of sentences. Click a number to see the page and the text in the document that match the answer.

sections.heading: What is asking about PDF documents
sections.body:
You can attach 1 to 5 of your own PDF files and ask about what is in them. When you attach a PDF, the system switches to **From documents** mode and answers only from the attached documents. It does not search other research and does not use the research field. The answer has numbers such as [1] and [2] at the end of sentences. Click a number to see the page and the text in the document that match the answer.

Use it to summarise a paper, ask about its methods or limits, or read work that is not in a public database.

sections.heading: How to ask about PDF documents
sections.body:
There are 2 ways

### Method 1 Attach the file in the question box

1. Click **Attach file** in the question box and choose a PDF file from your computer; its name appears above the question box

   ![Click Attach file in the question box and choose a PDF file from your computer; its name appears above the question box](/manual/en/docs-flow-1.webp#1280x800)

2. Enter your question about the document

   ![Enter your question about the document](/manual/en/docs-flow-2.webp#1280x800)

3. Click the paper-plane send button

   ![Click the paper-plane send button](/manual/en/docs-flow-3.webp#1280x800)

4. The system shows the answer from the document with a reference number

   ![The system shows the answer from the document with a reference number](/manual/en/docs-flow-4.webp#1280x800)

### Method 2 Pick a file already uploaded to **My files**

1. Click the actions button on the row of the PDF file

   ![Click the actions button on the row of the PDF file](/manual/en/docs-files-flow-1.webp#1280x800)

2. Choose **Ask about this document**

   ![Choose Ask about this document](/manual/en/docs-files-flow-2.webp#1280x800)

3. The system opens the chat with the file attached. Enter your question and click send

   ![The system opens the chat with the file attached. Enter your question and click send](/manual/en/docs-files-flow-3.webp#1280x800)

![Ask about an uploaded PDF](/manual/en/docs-video.mp4#cc "Ask about an uploaded PDF")

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.body:
- You cannot attach PDFs together with a data file. If you attach a data file, the system analyses the data instead. See [Analyze a data file](/docs/analyze-data)
- The system reads at most the first 300 pages of each file
- The **Reproduction plan** button, which appears when you attach a PDF, makes the system list what is needed to reproduce the paper: the main results, the data, the methods, the steps, and what the paper does not say. The system does not run any code
- The text of the attached documents is sent to the language model to write the answer, so do not attach documents that must not be disclosed. See [Where your data is kept and sent](/docs/data-and-privacy)
- An attached PDF also appears in **My files**. See [Upload and preview files](/docs/manage-files)
- Always check the answer against the document. The system quotes the text and gives the page so you can check

sections.heading: Problems and fixes
sections.body:
- **Problem:** “You can attach up to 5 PDFs”  
  **Fix:** Remove some attachments with **Remove file**, then attach again
- **Problem:** “Choose PDFs or one data file, not both”  
  **Fix:** Attach only PDFs, or only one data file
- **Problem:** “sample-paper.pdf could not be read as a PDF (it may be damaged or password-protected)”  
  **Fix:** Open the file in a PDF reader to check it, remove the password, then attach it again
- **Problem:** “sample-paper.pdf has no extractable text (it may be a scanned image)”  
  **Fix:** Use a file whose text can be selected, not a scanned image
- **Problem:** “The selected document was not found (it may have been deleted)”  
  **Fix:** Attach the PDF again
- **Problem:** “Asking about documents needs the server's shared database, which is not available”  
  **Fix:** Ask the server administrator to connect the shared database

sections.body:

topics.title: Analyze a data file
topics.summary: Attach a table file (CSV, XLSX, Parquet or JSON) and ask in plain language. The system writes and runs a Python script in a container with no internet, then shows the result as tables, charts and findings. Use it to compare groups, find averages or draw charts from your own data.

sections.heading: What is analyzing a data file
sections.body:
Attach a table file (CSV, XLSX, Parquet or JSON) and ask in plain language. The system writes and runs a Python script in a container with no internet, then shows the result as tables, charts and findings. Use it to compare groups, find averages or draw charts from your own data.

When a data file is attached, the send button analyses that data instead of searching the literature.

sections.heading: How to analyze a data file
sections.body:
1. Go to **My files** in the left bar

   ![Go to My files in the left bar](/manual/en/data-flow-1.webp#1280x800)

2. Click the actions button on the row of the data file

   ![Click the actions button on the row of the data file](/manual/en/data-flow-2.webp#1280x800)

3. Choose **Analyze**

   ![Choose Analyze](/manual/en/data-flow-3.webp#1280x800)

4. Enter your question about the attached data

   ![Enter your question about the attached data](/manual/en/data-flow-4.webp#1280x800)

5. Click the paper-plane send button

   ![Click the paper-plane send button](/manual/en/data-flow-5.webp#1280x800)

6. The system shows the analysis with tables and a chart

   ![The system shows the analysis with tables and a chart](/manual/en/data-flow-6.webp#1280x800)

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.body:
- The result has the tabs **Overview**, **Tables**, **Charts**, **Findings** and **Code and run log**, and a button to download the result table
- The system shows the stages it went through: profile the file, write the script, run the analysis, repair the script (if needed) and store the results
- A language model wrote the script. Before you use the numbers, open the **Code and run log** tab and check that it computed what you meant
- A table in the result may show only the first rows, and a very large file may be cut at the row limit. The system says so in the result
- You can ask only about the data in the file. To search the literature, remove the file first. See [Ask a research question](/docs/ask-a-question)
- You can also choose the same file from **My files** and click **Analyze**. See [Upload and preview files](/docs/manage-files)

sections.heading: Problems and fixes
sections.body:
- **Problem:** “This question is not about the uploaded data.”  
  **Fix:** Ask about the table in the file, for example compare the mean of each group
- **Problem:** “This is a literature question, not an analysis of the uploaded file.”  
  **Fix:** To search the literature, remove the file and ask again
- **Problem:** “File analysis is not enabled on this server”  
  **Fix:** Ask the server administrator to turn on file analysis
- **Problem:** “Could not upload the file”  
  **Fix:** Check that the file is a supported type and not damaged, then attach it again

sections.heading: Related questions
sections.body:
- [Upload and preview files](/docs/manage-files)
- [What the system covers and what you must check](/docs/limits-and-safety)

topics.title: Upload and preview files
topics.summary: The My files menu lists the files you uploaded, the files you attached in the question box, and the documents saved from a report. Each row shows the name, type, size, upload date and project. Use it to upload a file ahead of time, check what is in a file, or download it again.

sections.heading: What is uploading and previewing files
sections.body:
The **My files** menu lists the files you uploaded, the files you attached in the question box, and the documents saved from a report. Each row shows the name, type, size, upload date and project. Use it to upload a file ahead of time, check what is in a file, or download it again.

The menu of each file has **Preview**, **Download**, **Rename**, **Analyze** (data files) or **Ask about this document** (PDF), **Move to project** and **Delete**.

sections.heading: How to upload and preview files
sections.body:
1. Click **Upload a file** and choose a file from your computer; the system adds it to the list

   ![Click Upload a file and choose a file from your computer; the system adds it to the list](/manual/en/files-flow-1.webp#1280x800)

2. Click the actions button on the row of the file

   ![Click the actions button on the row of the file](/manual/en/files-flow-2.webp#1280x800)

3. Choose **Preview**

   ![Choose Preview](/manual/en/files-flow-3.webp#1280x800)

4. The system shows the first rows of the file in a preview window

   ![The system shows the first rows of the file in a preview window](/manual/en/files-flow-4.webp#1280x800)

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.body:
- You can upload CSV, XLSX, Parquet and JSON to analyse, and PDF to ask about documents
- The preview shows only the first rows of a table file
- You can rename a file. The new name must not be empty, must be at most 120 characters, and must keep the same extension
- Deleting a file moves it to the trash for 7 days, then removes it from storage for good. See [Restore an item from the trash](/docs/trash)
- Use the **Search files** box to find a file by name
- PDF and Word files saved from a report are listed here too. See [Create a report document from an answer](/docs/create-report)

sections.heading: Problems and fixes
sections.body:
- **Problem:** “The file is no longer in storage”  
  **Fix:** Click **Remove from list**, then upload the file again
- **Problem:** “File storage is unavailable right now. Try again later”  
  **Fix:** Wait a moment and try again
- **Problem:** “The file is too large to preview”  
  **Fix:** Download the file and open it in a program on your computer
- **Problem:** “No preview for this file type”  
  **Fix:** Download the file and open it in a program on your computer
- **Problem:** “The file extension must stay .csv”  
  **Fix:** Give the new name, keeping the same extension at the end
- **Problem:** “The name is longer than 120 characters”  
  **Fix:** Use a shorter name

sections.heading: Related questions
sections.body:
- [Analyze a data file](/docs/analyze-data)
- [Ask about PDF documents](/docs/ask-documents)
- [Restore an item from the trash](/docs/trash)

topics.title: Create a report document from an answer
topics.summary: From a finished answer, click Open report to open the Research report draft in the right panel. The panel has Contents to jump to a heading, Share & export to export at once as PDF, Word or Markdown or to copy the text, and Edit & create document, which opens a full-screen editor.

sections.heading: What is creating a report document
sections.body:
From a finished answer, click **Open report** to open the **Research report draft** in the right panel. The panel has **Contents** to jump to a heading, **Share & export** to export at once as PDF, Word or Markdown or to copy the text, and **Edit & create document**, which opens a full-screen editor.

Use the full-screen editor when you want to change the text, set the title, and choose the language, style and font before saving. A PDF or Word file you save is kept in **My files**.

sections.heading: How to create a report document from an answer
sections.body:
1. Click **Open report** below the answer

   ![Click Open report below the answer](/manual/en/report-flow-1.webp#1280x800)

2. Click **Edit & create document**

   ![Click Edit & create document](/manual/en/report-flow-2.webp#1280x800)

3. Edit the title and the text on the page as needed

   ![Edit the title and the text on the page as needed](/manual/en/report-flow-3.webp#1280x800)

4. Choose **Document language**

   ![Choose Document language](/manual/en/report-flow-4.webp#1280x800)

5. Choose **Document style**

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.body:
- Click **Preview PDF** to see the real PDF you will get in the chosen style. The Word file has the same content, but its look may differ from the preview
- When you change **Document language**, the system translates the content. If the translation fails, the original language and content stay
- **Document style** offers **Standard** and **Official**. The font is chosen in the same row
- The **Include references** switch adds the references built from the sources at the end of the document

sections.heading: Problems and fixes

- **Problem:** “A table has more than 12 columns or a cell over 500 characters. Shrink the table before making the file.”

- **Problem:** “Over the limit the server accepts. Remove sections or paragraphs before creating the file”

- **Problem:** “The document service is unavailable. Try again later; your form is kept”

- **Problem:** “Could not save the file. Nothing was added to My files. Try again; your form is kept”  
  **Fix:** Click the save button again
- **Problem:** “The preview could not be made. Check the title, sections and paragraphs”

sections.heading: What is adding paper details
sections.body:
The **Paper details** window in the document editor adds an outline, the authors, keywords, an abstract and the closing statements that journals and universities often require. Use it after you open the editor as in [Create a report document from an answer](/docs/create-report).

There are 5 paper types: **Research (IMRaD)**, **Computer science paper**, **Review article**, **Thai thesis, 5 chapters** and **Research proposal**. **Insert outline** adds only the headings that are not in the document yet, at the end. Text you already wrote is not changed or removed.

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.body:

- **Keywords**: separated by commas, up to 8
- **Abstract**: plain text, can be left empty. If you fill it in, it shows under the title
- **Closing statements** has 4 items: Use of generative AI, Data and code availability, Ethics, and Conflicts of interest. They appear before the references, only the ones you tick
- The starting text of each item is a neutral draft with square brackets [ ] to fill in. You must change it to match the facts before you use it
- Author names can be personal data. Enter only what you want to appear in the document

topics.title: Where your data is kept and sent
topics.summary: AI Scientist has no sign-in, so the chats, projects and files you create are not tied to a person. Where the server is connected to the shared database, all data is kept in that database, and everyone who can reach the same server sees and edits the same data. A status indicator sits at the bottom left of the sidebar.

sections.heading: Where your data is
sections.body:
AI Scientist has no sign-in, so the chats, projects and files you create are not tied to a person. Where the server is connected to the shared database, all data is kept in that database, and everyone who can reach the same server sees and edits the same data. A status indicator sits at the bottom left of the sidebar.

- “Online · shared database”: the data is in the shared database and synced
- “Offline · waiting to sync n items”: the server cannot be reached, but you can keep working. Changes sync when you are back online
- “Browser mode (no database)”: the data is kept only in this browser. The trash, usage and asking about documents do not work

sections.heading: What is sent off your computer
sections.body:
- The question and the text found are sent to the server and to an outside language model provider to write the answer, so do not put personal data in a question
- The text of an attached PDF is also sent to the model to answer
- The analysis of a data file runs in a container with no internet and with limits on time and memory, but the column names and the text in cells are sent to the model that writes the script as context
- The identifier check sends only the DOI, PMID or arXiv ID to Crossref, PubMed and arXiv
- The **Usage** page is a summary of real questions and answers on the server, and it does not keep the question text

sections.heading: Deleting data and old data in the browser
sections.body:
![The data section of the settings window](/manual/en/settings-data.webp#1280x800 "The data section of the settings window")

- **Delete all chats** in the **Data** section of the settings deletes all chats and projects in the shared database. Nobody who uses this server will see them again. The items stay in the trash for 7 days before they are deleted for good. The system asks you to confirm first. Read the whole confirmation before you press it
- An earlier version of the system kept chats in the browser. The **Earlier data in this browser** section says whether any was found. **Import to the shared database** imports it, and after the import everyone who can reach the server sees that data. You can press it again without creating duplicates
- If the browser storage is full, the system tells you to delete old chats

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.body: Because there is no sign-in, anyone who opens the same server can read your chats, files and trash. Do not keep confidential work or other people's personal data in this system. If you are not sure how your server is set up, ask the server administrator.

sections.heading: Example
sections.body: Two people open the same server. The first asks a question and uploads a data file. The second opens **My files** and sees that file too, and can open the first person's chat.

topics.title: What the system covers and what you must check
topics.summary: AI Scientist answers only scientific research questions, in Thai and English. It writes the answer only from the papers it finds. If the evidence is not enough, the answer says plainly that it cannot conclude. It does not guess.

sections.heading: What the system answers
sections.body: AI Scientist answers only scientific research questions, in Thai and English. It writes the answer only from the papers it finds. If the evidence is not enough, the answer says plainly that it cannot conclude. It does not guess.

sections.heading: What the system refuses
sections.body:
When it refuses, the screen shows a short message and sample questions so you can go back to a research topic. No search starts.

![A question the system does not answer](/manual/en/refused.webp#1280x800 "A question the system does not answer")

- **This question is outside this tool's scope**: a question that is not scientific research
- **This request tries to change the assistant's instructions, so it was not followed.**: text that tells the system to change its own rules
- **This cannot be done here (for example writing work for you, a diagnosis, or reading files and secrets).**
- In **Answer research** mode: if you ask something that needs a new search, or the chat has no results yet, the system tells you to switch the mode or search first
- In file analysis: a question that is not about the data in the file, or a literature question, is turned back and you are told to ask again

sections.heading: What you must check yourself
sections.body:
- The label that says the references were checked only confirms that the DOI, PMID or arXiv ID exists. It does not confirm that the paper supports the sentence it is cited for
- The reviewer reads only the abstract, not the full text. So “Supported by the abstract” does not certify that the paper really supports it
- A reference without a DOI, PMID or arXiv ID cannot be checked by identifier, and a reference that “could not be checked” may only mean the checking service did not answer
- The language model can still be wrong. Open the original before you use it. See [Open the sources of an answer](/docs/read-sources)
- If you stop the work before it ends, the answer is incomplete. The system says so in the answer
- A file analysis comes from a script the model wrote. Check it in the **Code and run log** tab. See [Analyze a data file](/docs/analyze-data)
- The closing statements of a report are neutral drafts. The author must change them to match the facts. See [Add the paper type, authors and closing statements](/docs/report-details)
- The author is responsible for the content of the exported report

sections.heading: Limits to know
sections.body:
- A question is at most 2000 characters
- At most 5 search terms per question, and each search term can take up to 5 minutes
- You can attach up to 5 PDFs, and the system reads the first 300 pages of each
- When several people use the system, work waits in a queue
- The system does not run code from attached documents, and file analysis has no internet

topics.summary: The problem messages you meet most often when you use AI Scientist, and how to fix them. Look for the message you see on the screen in the list below. Problems that belong to one task are on the page of that task, such as Ask about PDF documents and Create a report document from an answer.

sections.body: The problem messages you meet most often when you use AI Scientist, and how to fix them. Look for the message you see on the screen in the list below. Problems that belong to one task are on the page of that task, such as [Ask about PDF documents](/docs/ask-documents) and [Create a report document from an answer](/docs/create-report).

sections.heading: Problems and fixes
sections.body:
- **Problem:** “Could not reach the server”  
  **Fix:** Check your internet connection and that the server is running, then reload the page. If it still fails, tell the server administrator
- **Problem:** “The connection ended before the answer was complete”  
  **Fix:** The answer is incomplete. Click **Try again** to ask again
- **Problem:** “Received unreadable data from the server”  
  **Fix:** Ask again. If it stays the same, tell the server administrator
- **Problem:** “Request failed”  
  **Fix:** Try again. If it keeps happening, tell the server administrator
- **Problem:** “Could not start the run. Try again.”  
  **Fix:** Send the question again
- **Problem:** “Not sure the question reached the server. If it did, it will appear in this chat. Check before sending it again.”  
  **Fix:** Wait a moment and look in this chat to see whether the question appears. Send it again only when you are sure it did not, so it does not search twice
- **Problem:** “The server queues this run. Reload the page and try again.”  
  **Fix:** Reload the page, then send the question again
- **Problem:** “Another research run is in progress”  
  **Fix:** Wait for that work to finish, or click **Stop** on it
- **Problem:** “Could not stop the run. Try again.”  
  **Fix:** Click **Stop** again
- **Problem:** “The run was interrupted (for example by a reload). You can retry.”  
  **Fix:** Click **Try again**
- **Problem:** “No papers yet. Each search can take up to 5 minutes, and some external databases answer slowly or limit requests.”  
  **Fix:** Keep waiting. The system is still working. If you do not want to wait, click **Stop**
- **Problem:** “This question is outside this tool's scope”  
  **Fix:** Ask a scientific research question. See [What the system covers and what you must check](/docs/limits-and-safety)
- **Problem:** “The scope check could not be completed. Please try again.”  
  **Fix:** Send the question again
- **Problem:** “The question is too long. Please shorten it.”  
  **Fix:** Shorten the question
- **Problem:** “There are no search results in this session to answer from yet. Run a search first.”  
  **Fix:** Change the mode to **Deep research** or **General search** and get an answer first, then use **Answer research**
- **Problem:** “Browser storage is full. Delete old chats; new chats may not be saved.”  
  **Fix:** Delete old chats you no longer use. See [Delete a chat](/docs/delete-chat)
- **Problem:** “The sync queue is full, so some edits may not be saved. Try reconnecting.”  
  **Fix:** Check the connection to the server, then reload the page and check that your latest edits are still there
- **Problem:** “Someone else changed this item. We loaded the latest version.”  
  **Fix:** Someone else edited the same item. Check that it is what you want, and do it again if needed
- **Problem:** “This page failed to render. Try again; your chats stored in this browser are not affected.”  
  **Fix:** Click **Try again** or reload the page
